lines: {target}? Sound travels farther than sense. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Deep Dark, tell them. Walk soft and do not open every chest. I will be at the bell.
Sculk hears what pride forgets. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Deep Dark is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I'll remember Deep Dark as darkness that listens back. I'll stay where I can hear the bell.
Noticing a warden in the dark would end my curiosity quickly. I like curiosity, but I like distance more.
I would ask whether the prize was worth walking past a warden in the dark. That feels like a short discussion.
At Deep Dark, I would measure distance in snacks. Three snacks is not nearby.
I would not trade the last loaf for a souvenir from Deep Dark. Please remind me I said that.
I would not decide that shriekers answering nearby meant no trouble at Deep Dark without asking someone else.
I would wave at Deep Dark when leaving. I wave at places sometimes. They rarely wave back.
I may not lead a rescue well at Deep Dark, but I can run home and ring the bell with real commitment.
At Deep Dark, a short rest near the last quiet tunnel might prevent a very long mistake.
I have packed for trips before. This time I would remember wool, food, and patience before a spoon.
The village has fewer surprises than Deep Dark. This is one of its finest qualities.
A trip to Deep Dark is no time to discover my left boot has become adventurous.
On the way back from Deep Dark, I would follow our marks instead of inventing a better route.
Conditions like complete darkness could change the whole trip to Deep Dark. I would rather notice early.
Nothing I carried home from Deep Dark should make the return dangerous.
Maps and I have an agreement. They show the route and I ask a nearby person what it means.
{target}? Stone teeth hang above and wait below. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Dripstone Caves, tell them. Look up as often as you look down. I will be at the bell.
Pointed stone makes every stumble serious. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Dripstone Caves is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Dripstone Caves as a cave that bites from both directions. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
I have no clever trick for a creeper behind the columns. Leaving is a trick I can usually manage.
People may admire dripstone. I would first ask whether it was safe to stand on.
There are probably answers in Dripstone Caves. I would be happy just to make it back outside.
Nobody earns a prize for stepping on sharp dripstone.
I would wait for a careful plan before entering Dripstone Caves. Bread helps me wait.
After seeing dripstone, plain packed dirt might look quite elegant.
Good boots matter in Dripstone Caves. Mine would announce every step to the cave.
I remember places by smells I cannot describe. Dripstone Caves sounds likely to become one.
A blind rescue through pointed stone only gives the cave two lost travelers.
I would choose a safe place to rest. I should probably ask whether it is safe first.
I pack bread for danger and carrots for thinking. Neither is clever, but both fit in a pack.
For Dripstone Caves, I would pack torches, food, sturdy boots, and one useless thing for luck.
People make dripstone sound impressive. I mostly hear a difficult walk home.
The shiny things can stay in Dripstone Caves. I have nowhere sensible for dripping cave treasure.
A safe Dripstone Caves story should end under open sky.
{target}? Pretty caves still have long drops. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Lush Caves, tell them. Watch the vines and the holes between them. I will be at the bell.
Glow berries light paths that may not be safe. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Lush Caves is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Lush Caves as a cave trying very hard to look harmless. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
A trip to Lush Caves is no time to discover my left boot has become adventurous.
At Lush Caves, I would listen when someone said I was going the wrong way. Eventually.
Lush Caves might look close from the tunnel with daylight air. Places lie about distance when I am tired.
Seeing a zombie behind the glow berries would remind me of an urgent appointment somewhere behind me.
I do not need every shiny thing near the vines below ground. I have nowhere sensible to put most of them.
A story about Lush Caves needs a safe ending. Otherwise it is a warning with names.
If I heard water running through leaves, I would listen before deciding it was harmless. That is a new habit.
There are probably answers at Lush Caves. I would settle for returning with the questions.
I pack bread for danger and carrots for thinking. I am not sure either works, but they travel well.
I would leave Lush Caves before dark made the vines below ground harder to read.
Lush Caves sounds impressive when people mention the vines below ground. The trip home sounds less impressive.
I would point at the tunnel with daylight air three times and still ask whether everyone saw it.
I have packed for trips before. This time I would remember torches, food, and a water bucket before a spoon.
Nobody puts smells on a map. That seems careless when a bad smell can find you first.
I would return before people had to wonder where I wandered. They do enough of that.
